title: Daemon
description:
A declarative description of a daemon: the system user/group it runs
as, the directories it needs, its binary, its systemd unit, and
(optionally) a seed config file — everything [`Daemon::install`] needs
to set the daemon up, and [`Daemon::uninstall`] needs to tear it back
down.

`Daemon` implements [`Serialize`]/[`Deserialize`], so it can be loaded
from a config file (TOML, JSON, or anything else `serde` supports)
instead of being built by hand — see `examples/install_daemon_from_toml.rs`.

binary.description: The daemon binary to copy into place.

bootstrap.description:
A seed config file, written once on first install and never
overwritten or removed if it already existed beforehand.

directories.description: Directories to create, each anchored under a [`DaemonPath`] root.

help.description:
Printed after a successful install (e.g. next-step instructions for
the person running it).

users.description:
Users to create. Each user's `belongs_to` groups are also added as
members during install.

Binary.description:
The daemon's executable, copied from `src` to `dest` and made
world-executable (`0o755`).

dst.description: Path to copy the binary to (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/mydaemon`).

name.description:
Identifying name for this binary. Not currently used to resolve any
path — `src`/`dst` are used directly.

src.description: Path to copy the binary from (e.g. a local build output).

Bootstrap.description:
A single seed file, written to `<kind's root>/<dir_name>/<file_name>` and
left alone on every subsequent install (or uninstall) if it already existed
— this crate never overwrites or deletes config a daemon or its administrator
may have since edited.

configs.description:
Configs to be written the first time the file is created. Ignored if the
file already exists.

path.description: Which FHS root the file is created under.

DaemonPath.description: A directory anchored under one of the standard FHS roots.

oneOf.description: `/run/<rest of path>` — runtime state (pid files, sockets)

Directory.description:
A single directory a daemon needs, resolved to `<kind's root>/<name>`
(e.g. `DaemonPath::State` + `"myapp"` → `/var/lib/myapp`).

path.description: Which FHS root this directory is created under.

Group.description: A system group, identified by name.

RelativePath.description:
A path that's been checked to be relative and free of `..` traversal.
The only way to get one is [`RelativePath::new`] (or `Deserialize`,
which calls it) — the inner `PathBuf` is private, so there's no way to
construct a `RelativePath` that skipped the check. Having one at all
*is* the proof it's valid.

name.description:
The unit name (without `.service`) — also used directly as the
`systemctl` target for start/stop/restart/disable.

User.description:
A system user, created as a system account with no home directory and a
`nologin` shell — daemons don't need interactive login.

belongs_to.description: Groups this user is added to as a member during [`Daemon::install`](crate::Daemon::install).
